transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-17
Start time: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (BrightKey - Head of ML), Lena Ortiz (BrightKey - Platform Eng), Grace Kim (BrightKey - Product)

Summary: quick review of this week's POC results; discuss model selection and pinning strategy; confirm rollback/fallback runbook and next steps for canary tests. Some noise on line, a few dropped words in places.

Topics: model selection (cost vs latency), pinning to catalog versions, canary rollbacks, fallback to smaller model, KV/prefix caching impacts, quantization profiles, "Dedicated" test pool stability.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll get started. I see Samir, Lena, Grace - thanks for making time. Priya and I are here to walk through the latest numbers and confirm the pinning and rollback plan.
[00:18] Samir: Yep, thanks. We had a couple infra things earlier but should be fine now. Quick ask, can we keep this to 45 ish minutes and then open Q/A?
[00:25] Jordan: Sure, we'll aim for that. 
[00:30] Priya: I'll share my screen for the perf tables - apologies if the screen share lags, our connection is a little spotty today.
[00:38] Grace: No worries.
[00:40] Priya: OK so first slide, baseline: we ran the brightkey-summarization test across three candidates from the Redwood catalog - Model-A v1.2.3 (larger, higher quality), Model-B v2.0.1 (mid-size, quantized) and Model-C v0.9.7 (low-cost fallback). The p50/p95 latency numbers on Dedicated dev pool are here — p50 for A ~180ms, p95 ~420ms; B p50 ~120ms p95 ~300ms; C p50 ~80ms p95 ~220ms. Token cost per 1k tokens: A ~$0.12, B ~$0.07, C ~$0.03 (these are normalized internal numbers).
[01:35] Samir: Those look good. The product team is sensitive to p95 under 400ms for interactive flows, but in some cases we can tolerate up to 500 if quality is significantly better. We're also tracking hallucination rate in the eval harness.
[01:50] Jordan: Right, and on hallucination/quality we ran your 200 prompt eval set. Model-A had a 3.6% critical hallucination rate, Model-B 4.8%, Model-C 9.9% — Model-A is noticeably better on QA completions.
[02:10] Lena: Quick question, the p95 numbers, are they with KV cache warm? Last week our p95 spiked because the key value cache was cold and we had a high prefix length.
[02:20] Priya: Good call. The table is mixed - some runs were warm, some cold. I added a column for warm cache runs — with warm KV cache Model-A p95 drops to ~300ms, Model-B ~220ms. So cache helps a lot for repeated user sessions.
[02:40] Grace: So for pinning, are we proposing pin to Model-A by default and fallback to Model-B or C under pressure?
[02:48] Jordan: That's the current recommendation: pin to Model-A v1.2.3 for the main route to meet quality targets, but configure routing policy to fallback to Model-B v2.0.1 for cost-sensitive or capacity constrained cases, and Model-C as last-resort. Also we recommend canary pinning first (10% traffic to new pin) and monitor quality/regressions.
[03:10] Samir: How automated is the fallback? Can Redwood route automatically if Dedicated pool CPU/GPU utilization hits X%? 
[03:18] Priya: Yes — our Smart Routing policies can route by metric thresholds (latency, GPU queue length, region). We can set a rule like if avg GPU queue depth > 0.6 or p95 > 450ms then route to fallback. There's also an automatic rollback trigger if regression detectors fire during canary.
[03:36] Samir: Nice, would want to see the exact webhook and alert flows.
[03:40] Jordan: We'll share the runbook with webhook examples. Priya, can you confirm the rollback steps live?
[03:45] Priya: Sure. Rollback playbook: 1) Pause traffic to canary (immediate), 2) Re-route to previous pinned version (we maintain stable pin history), 3) Run perf check on a sample window, 4) Open a ticket in BrightKey's SRE channel and escalate if needed. The entire reversal should be sub-2 minutes for control-plane step, plus propagation to edge - so realistically 3-7 minutes.
[04:14] Lena: That's acceptable. The sub-5 minute SLA is good. One concern: we need a test for partial degradation (quality drop but latency OK) — automatic rollback based solely on latency might not catch that.
[04:28] Priya: Correct — we have regression detectors based on eval prompts and safety checks. For POC we recommend tethering a small eval set that runs through canary traffic and triggers alerts if hallucination > threshold. We can wire that into the same policy.
[04:45] Grace: Can you give an example of the pinning config? I'm imagining an API call we would run as part of our deploy.
[04:52] Priya: Absolutely. Example: POST /routes/{route_id}/pin with body { model: "Model-A", version: "1.2.3", traffic_split: { stable: 90, canary: 10 }, fallback: [ { model: "Model-B", version:"2.0.1" }, { model: "Model-C", version:"0.9.7" } ], triggers: { queueDepth: 0.6, p95: 450 } } — I'm paraphrasing, the actual schema will be in the runbook I send.
[05:22] Samir: Good — that looks like what we need. Another question: quantization — we saw Model-B was quantized in your runs, how much quality delta should we expect if we change quant profile?
[05:34] Priya: For B, we tested 8-bit quant with per-channel quantization which gave minimal quality hit for most of your prompts (~0.5% increase in hallucination). 4-bit aggressive quant starts to show bigger regressions in LLM QA tasks. We can recommend B as 8-bit for cost/latency sweet spot.
[05:50] Grace: And for Dedicated do we get the same quant benefits?
[05:53] Priya: Yes, quant is model-level, not infra-level — runtime supports quant kernels; you get the performance improvements on Dedicated too.
[06:01] Lena: We had a flake last week where the Dedicated dev pool had GPU driver mismatch after an infra patch and we saw p50 doubles for short window, does Redwood surface those kernel/driver issues?
[06:12] Jordan: We capture infra signals and expose them in the Console — you get per-pod metrics, kernel mismatches show up as degraded utilization and error rates. For POC we'll also provide a health-check dashboard link.
[06:23] Samir: Nice. On pricing: can you confirm what the incremental cost looks like for Model-A pinned vs Model-B? You mentioned earlier token cost, but curious about committed vs burst pricing on Dedicated.
[06:34] Jordan: Short answer: Model-A costs ~1.7x per token on our unit numbers compared to Model-B; however Dedicated capacity amortizes GPU hour cost — the marginal token cost on Dedicated depends on utilization. For the POC we can give you a modeled projection in the spreadsheet we'll send.
[06:52] Grace: One more practical: during canary we want to run a small human review set on outputs to double-check for subtle regressions. Can we route 1% of traffic to a human review queue?
[07:03] Priya: Yup, Redwood supports sampling rules to mirror a fraction of traffic into your audit queue or to a shadow endpoint. We can set that up.
[07:12] Lena: About security and data residency — can the pinning config be applied in your Private deployment? We need control plane in our VPC for production later.
[07:22] Jordan: Yes — the same pinning API exists in Private deployments; the control plane calls are proxied locally. For POC we're on Hosted Dedicated dev pool, but we can demo Private later.
[07:33] Samir: OK — I think we're aligned on model-A pin, fallback B then C, canary first. Let's talk about the rollback test next week.
[07:41] Jordan: Proposed schedule: next Wed (2025-11-24) we do a 1-hour canary window where BrightKey will run their interactive traffic and we will intentionally simulate a regression in the canary to validate rollback. Does that work?
[07:52] Lena: Works for us — I'll provision the dev Dedicated pool and give access.
[07:57] Grace: I'll coordinate the human review cohort.
[08:01] Samir: I'll finalize success criteria: p95 < 450ms OR hallucination < 5% for the route; otherwise rollback.
[08:10] Jordan: Great. A few notes from the chat — Priya posted the perf link and the baseline CSV.
[08:16] Priya: Quick caveat: some of the transcriptions here use model labels that might be auto-corrected by the transcript engine — Model-A etc are our shorthand. The actual catalog IDs are in the spreadsheet.
[08:30] Grace: Anything else on tuning?
[08:33] Priya: We recommend enabling prefix KV caching for sessions where users have repeated history; that reduces p95 dramatically for multi-turn flows. Also suggest session-level cache TTL of 30 minutes for interactive apps.
[08:48] Samir: Is there a risk of stale cache causing hallucinations?
[08:51] Priya: Not hallucinations per se, but stale context can degrade relevance. We usually combine a freshness tag and light re-query policy. We can include sample code.
[09:02] Jordan: Ok wrapping up — let's restate next steps. Jordan will send updated pricing/benchmark spreadsheet (action item). Priya will share pinning & rollback runbook and example API bodies. BrightKey will provision the dev Dedicated pool and confirm success criteria. We schedule the canary test for 2025-11-24.
[09:25] Grace: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[09:28] Samir: Thanks, appreciate it.
[09:30] Jordan: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links.

End of transcript.

References/links mentioned in call: perf spreadsheet (link posted in chat), runbook (will be shared), console health dashboard (link).
